name: Why did my new bathroom floor fail again after only a few years?

mainEntity.name: Why did my new bathroom floor fail again after only a few years?

acceptedAnswer.text: A bathroom floor can fail again when the leak remains active, the subfloor moves, the surface was installed over an unsuitable base, perimeter details are weak, or the toilet seal and transitions were not handled correctly. Ask for the cause of the original failure, not just a recommendation for a different finish material. Have the installer explain substrate preparation, moisture control, movement accommodation, and fixture detailing. Elite Remodeling & Design can coordinate those items when flooring is part of a complete bathroom renovation.
acceptedAnswer.description: Repeat failure often comes from an unresolved leak, movement in the subfloor, poor preparation, weak perimeter details, or an improperly handled toilet seal—not simply the flooring product. Before replacing it again, identify the original failure mechanism and ask how the new installation will correct that specific cause.
